purpose: Non-windowed verification of Rust profile management state, validation, stable-ID selection, deletion confirmation and static text/column integration; GUI and performance acceptance deferred

concurrent_workspace_context.note: An independent network-policy task changed the global component updater and Python overlay test during verification. This UI commit excludes those files; the current shared framework was rebuilt with the following patch snapshot. Python count includes one concurrent overlay test. UI source matching covers source_sha256 only.

build_consistency: final Ninja dry run reported no work to do

deferred_gui_matrix.note: Run each matrix in an isolated browser fixture with the matching backend; listing and compilation do not establish a pass.

unit_verified_mechanisms: Stable profile-ID selection follows reorder, removal and newly added profiles. Missing selection cannot rename/delete.

Controls and action admission reject unready/busy/duplicate submission, used-profile deletion and last-profile deletion. Both deletion clicks recheck safety; selected identity, catalogue, busy or usage changes disarm confirmation.
Create/rename trim Unicode whitespace, reject empty/ASCII-case-insensitive duplicate names and preserve Unicode. Rename retains its own ID and create-and-attach rejects a vanished workspace.
Service-specific status survives accepted/rejected admission. Generic rejection remains retryable; UI admission is separate from durable storage completion.
Paragraph geometry preserves every supplied line and its extent; generic text scene primitives now retain requested bold weight without changing the quad ABI.
implemented_pending_runtime_verification: Rust supplies panel copy, state, status, button readiness/delete caption, stable-ID catalogue reconciliation and typed create/rename/delete requests. Application callbacks retain profile creation/leases/directories/assignment/persistence/rollback.

Static panel text uses CoreText regular/medium shaping, Rust paragraph placement and clipped Metal surfaces sharing the existing context. Native fallback paints the same recipe. Typography caches invalidate by text/width/font; existing scene fingerprints skip unchanged submissions.

The panel consumes the existing Rust column adapter with its original 20-point interior padding and one-point rounded border. Native editor/picker/buttons and outer popup placement/focus/lifetime remain.
Native IME composition gates actions. Controls refresh after synchronous service callbacks and later busy updates; validation/service feedback survives that refresh.

The compiled regression covers GPU title/static AX nodes, absence of panel-owned native Labels, used-profile guard, empty/duplicate names, IME composition, Unicode create/rename, same-target confirmation, catalogue-change disarming and actual deletion. It has not run.
deferred_checkpoint: Run all 53 curated Metal cases and 24 Views controls. Added existing profile lifecycle, workspace assignment, profile menu and failed-configuration-write cases cover service behavior beyond the new panel regression.
Verify actual typography, long names/help/status paragraphs, clipping/overlap, narrow screens, theme/scale, bold metrics and native/Metal fallback/teardown.
Verify keyboard/IME/focus/accessibility, disabled controls, reopening/selecting/reordering profiles, create-and-attach context and destructive confirmation cancellation/stale targets.
Verify persistent profile/session isolation, async errors/retry/rollback, deletion cleanup and durable restore; package/sign and inspect the matching isolated application.
Measure CPU/GPU and actual presentation separately against Views. Unit durations, compilation and drawable lifecycle hooks establish no speedup.
limitations: No window or browser test was launched. CoreText/Metal/native-input behavior was compiled but not exercised; unit tests use supplied typography metrics.
Native input/picker/button controls and popup presentation remain, along with other Views surfaces. Full migration is incomplete.
No crate, framework or other binary dependency was added. Existing original-code Apache-2.0 and required upstream notices are unchanged.
